newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO blasts climate change proposals.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO blasts climate change proposals.

text.p: Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton on Wednesday warned that Americans would lose jobs if the United States agreed to international restrictions on fossil fuels that were not imposed on developing nations.
In a speech, Eaton blasted international proposals to stem global warming by requiring industrialized countries to cut their carbon emissions after the year 2000.
If countries such as China or Mexico were not required to comply with such restrictions, they would gain jobs and overall worldwide emissions will not be reduced, he said.

The Clinton administration's plan would delay restrictions until after 2010. The proposal is one of many that are being discussed in international negotiations to reduce global warming, which culminate in Kyoto, Japan, in December.
None of the proposals under discussion would place restrictions on developing nations.
"As the price of energy is driven up in the United States by this treaty, jobs will inevitably migrate to developing countries where cheap fossil fuels will be readily available," Eaton said.

Chrysler sold a record 2.45 million vehicles last year, with more than 66 percent of them light trucks, minivans and sport/utility vehicles, which generally use more gasoline than passenger cars. Trucks are expected to make up an even bigger percentage of Chrysler's 1997 sales.

"Our side is naive. They think the issue is environment," Eaton said. "They'll be sitting across the table from other people who are savvy -- they know that the issue is jobs. Savvy people usually beat naive people in negotiations like that."
Eaton said there was "no proof" of a looming greenhouse gas crisis. If the threat was real, industrialized nations would have plenty of time to do something about it, he said.

"Stumbling around in the dark and overreacting now won't help," Eaton said. "And neither would shutting down relatively clean factories in the United States and Europe while permitting the whole Third World to put up a dirty, coal-fired industrial infrastructure like what we had 50 years ago."
Eaton made the speech after accepting Automotive Industries magazine's Executive of the Year award on Wednesday.
